Definition: reflexive of G681; properly, to attach oneself to, i.e. to touch (in many implied relations):--touch.
BiblicalUsage: Haptomai is the middle voice of the verb to touch, the form the Gospels use when someone reaches out and takes hold. In Matthew 8:3 Jesus puts forth his hand and touches the leper, in Matthew 9:20 the woman touches the hem of his garment, and in John 20:17 the risen Jesus tells Mary, touch me not.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the touch is the point: Jesus did not heal from a distance, and the woman did not wait for permission to reach for him.
